lead.hed: USNI: TACDEMO teams resume air shows; Growler unit stays grounded
lead.insight: USNI, Wednesday: Naval Air Forces told the outlet some tactical demonstration teams are back on the air-show circuit. All TACDEMO teams except the Growler demo team have been cleared since June 10, said Cmdr. Amelia Umayam, a Naval Air Forces spokesperson. The Growler team remains grounded. The Navy did not publish a return date for that unit.

political.hed: USNI: U.S., Norway, and Britain open drills on Jan Mayen
political.insight: USNI, Wednesday: U.S., Norwegian, and British forces deployed to Jan Mayen for Operation Atlantic City, a NATO Arctic Sentry drill that runs through Sept. 4. A MARFOREUR/AF release says the island sits north of the Greenland-Iceland-U.K. gap. U.S. units include II MEF, 10th Marines, and a New Hampshire Guard HIMARS platoon.

political.hed: SOUTHCOM: four killed in a Caribbean go-fast strike
political.insight: U.S. Southern Command said Tuesday that Joint Task Force Western Hemisphere struck a go-fast vessel on a known Caribbean trafficking route and killed four people it called narco-terrorists. Gen. Francis L. Donovan said the task force will keep hunting those networks. SOUTHCOM cited confirmed intelligence and did not publish cargo recovered from the boat.

political.hed: Defense News: Italy asks Brussels for €8 billion in defense loans
political.insight: Defense News, Wednesday from Rome: Italy asked the EU’s SAFE fund for €8 billion in cheap defense loans, down from a planned €14.9 billion. A source familiar with the talks confirmed the request. Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni’s coalition had delayed for months. The report does not say when Brussels will decide.

tech.hed: Defense News: the Army wants 8,000 short-range missiles a year
tech.insight: Defense News, Wednesday: the Army posted a sources-sought notice for a Hellfire-class missile that can fire from an M299 or equivalent launcher. Industry replies are due Sept. 15. After award, the first batch of up to 8,000 rounds is due in two years, then up to 8,000 a year. The notice wants an active production line.

tech.hed: UK: MBDA may share SCALP parts data so Ukraine can assemble
tech.insight: The British government said Monday that MBDA may release classified data on U.K. parts of the SCALP cruise missile so Ukraine and France can assemble the weapon in Ukraine. Defense News, Wednesday: Kyiv now has the licenses, but wartime factories are unlikely to turn out large numbers soon. No first-delivery date was published.

culture.hed: WORLD: Scott’s Dog Stars has the landscape, not the focus
culture.insight: WORLD, Tuesday: Ridley Scott’s The Dog Stars, from Peter Heller’s 2012 novel, follows Hig (Jacob Elordi) and Bangley (Josh Brolin) in a virus-emptied 2035 Colorado. The review credits striking mountain photography and says the script turns episodic, with a jarring third-act shift. The film is rated R for language and strong violence.

watch.hed: WATCH: Lincoln is still weeks from a 295-day mark
watch.insight: USNI reported Tuesday that USS Abraham Lincoln (CVN-72) is weeks from a 295-day mark on Sept. 12, which would be the second-longest carrier deployment since the Cold War, behind only USS Gerald R. Ford’s cruise that ended in May. As of Tuesday, Lincoln and Carrier Air Wing 9 were in the Indian Ocean. The Navy has not published a homecoming date.
